report.headline: The pelacarsen Phase 3 Lp(a)HORIZON trial did not meet its primary endpoint of reducing major cardiovascular events, consistent with a projected 11.3% relative risk reduction that yielded only 47.2% statistical power.
report.summary: The trial randomized 8,323 patients with established cardiovascular disease and Lp(a) ≥70 mg/dL to pelacarsen or placebo, targeting 993 primary endpoint events. The calculator projected an 11.3% relative risk reduction (HR 0.887) based on a 58.9% Lp(a) reduction from a 40 mg dose and a 19% LDL-C reduction from an 80 mg dose, far below the 16.3% reduction (HR 0.837) needed for 80% power. Median follow-up was 2.5 years versus a planned 4 years, further reducing power. The top-line readout states the primary endpoint was not met. Human genetics strongly support LPA as a causal target (Open Targets score 0.922, multiple variants with ORs 1.51–2.57 for coronary disease), so failure likely reflects an effect size too small to detect with the chosen sample and duration. Phase 3 safety data from FRONTIERS APHERESIS showed mostly mild injection site erythema at the 80 mg dose.

report.what_would_change_this: Publication of the observed hazard ratio, confidence interval, and component-specific results would confirm the magnitude and precision of the treatment effect; phase 3 on-treatment Lp(a) and LDL-C reductions at the HORIZON 80 mg dose and mean baseline Lp(a) would clarify whether the effect was too small or the trial underpowered.
report.readthrough_note: Olpasiran, an LPA-targeting siRNA in Phase 3 (NCT07136012, 11,000 patients, primary completion expected 2031), achieved 71–97% Lp(a) reduction in Phase 1 and may test whether larger Lp(a) lowering translates to cardiovascular benefit.

mechanism.notes: Phase 3 dose is 80 mg monthly; phase 2 data at 40 mg used as closest available. FRONTIERS APHERESIS (phase 3, 80 mg) showed -72% Lp(a) reduction (f_41e180cd554aed), suggesting actual phase 3 effect may be larger. for.text: Calculator predicts only 11.3% relative risk reduction (expected HR 0.887) with 47.2% power, well below the 80% power target; minimum detectable effect at 80% power is HR 0.837 (16.3% RRR).

Phase 2 Lp(a) reduction at 40 mg monthly is -58.9% (placebo-adjusted, Day 30); phase 3 dose is 80 mg monthly, but no verified phase 3 on-treatment Lp(a) reduction for HORIZON (f_1abf5bdbf602f1: None not stated).
FRONTIERS APHERESIS (phase 3, 80 mg every 4 weeks) showed -72% Lp(a) reduction at week 52, suggesting phase 3 dose may achieve greater lowering than the phase 2 40 mg data used in calculator.
Phase 2 LDL-C reduction -19% (placebo-adjusted) and -8.0 mg/dL absolute contribute to the LDL-equivalent estimate (0.613 mmol/L total).
Planned 993 events with 3.25-year median follow-up (midpoint of 2.5-year minimum and 4-year planned) yields only 47% power for the expected effect.

against.text: If actual phase 3 Lp(a) reduction at 80 mg matches FRONTIERS APHERESIS (-72%) and mean baseline Lp(a) exceeds the 70 mg/dL threshold, the absolute Lp(a) reduction and expected benefit would be larger.
Genetic evidence strongly supports LPA causality for coronary disease (genetic association score 0.922, multiple MR studies with ORs 1.49-3.67 per allele).

hypotheses.would_settle: Actual phase 3 on-treatment Lp(a) reduction at 80 mg in HORIZON, mean baseline Lp(a) in randomized cohort, and observed HR when trial reads out.

Phase 2 LDL-C changes (pmid:35300814) do not specify pelacarsen dose in the verified facts; dose for -19% / -8.0 mg/dL unclear.
No observed HR or CI available yet; trial readout pending.

issues.issue: design_or_endpoint hypothesis states 'This may be insufficient to capture full benefit of Lp(a) lowering on atherosclerotic progression' without supporting evidence. This is speculative.

This is an unsubstantiated claim requiring either supporting fact references or removal.

issues.issue: execution_or_nonscientific hypothesis 'against' claim states 'No conduct issues (adherence, dropout, crossover, protocol deviations) reported in available facts' with empty refs []. The cited refs (f_9aa35ffeabce05, f_af9f4873c81153, f_dc1fe6207219f9) only show randomization numbers, not conduct metrics. issues.issue: off_target_harm hypothesis references fact f_7c165c1ddfd91b ('no cardiovascular harm signal reported in phase 2') which is NOT in the current verified facts list. issues.issue: Calculator input uses Lp(a) baseline = 70 mg/dL (inclusion threshold) but mean baseline in randomized cohort is unknown. The method field notes this, but the baseline value directly affects absolute Lp(a) reduction calculation. FRONTIERS APHERESIS phase 3 baseline was 85.4 mg/dL (f_08d23d78598f9), suggesting HORIZON mean may be higher.

issues.issue: Calculator input uses LDL-C change -19% / -8.0 mg/dL from phase 2 (pmid:35300814) but verified facts do not specify which pelacarsen dose this corresponds to. The same paper reports -2% / -0.7 mg/dL as lower range. Dose uncertainty affects LDL-equivalent estimate.
issues.request: Search for dose-specific LDL-C changes in phase 2 pelacarsen data. If dose unclear, note as assumption and consider range (-2% to -19%) in sensitivity.

issues.issue: Calculator followup_years = 3.25 (midpoint of 2.5 min and 4 planned). Verifier contradicted f_aa53dba69890b4: source states 'minimum follow-up required to be 2.5 years' not median. The 3.25 value is an analyst estimate per instructions, but should be explicitly labeled as estimated midpoint, not reported median.
issues.request: Add calculator assumption: 'followup_years 3.25 is estimated midpoint of minimum 2.5y and planned ~4y; actual median follow-up unknown.'

issues.issue: population hypothesis 'for' point infers 'if mean baseline substantially above 70 mg/dL, absolute Lp(a) reduction would be larger and expected benefit greater' but refs (f_1db6503f0913df, f_8246e5fce02eee, f_6881260218b455) only show inclusion thresholds, not mean baseline. This is reasonable inference but should be labeled as such.
issues.request: Rephrase to clarify this is inference from threshold, not observed data. Add to would_settle: 'Mean baseline Lp(a) in randomized cohort.'

issues.issue: Multiple hypotheses reference 'prior analyses' or 'prior answers' (e.g., UTI imbalance, FRONTIERS -72% Lp(a) reduction) without ensuring those facts are in current verified set. FRONTIERS -72% is verified (f_41e180cd554aed) but UTI imbalance is not.
